¿Cómo se calculan el alcance y la altura: How are the range and maximum height of a projectile calculated?
Alcance R = v₀²·sen 2θ/g (máximo a 45°): Range R = v₀²·sin 2θ/g (maximum at 45°) and maximum height h = v₀²·sin²θ/(2g). With v₀ = 20 m/s and θ = 45°: R = 400/9.8 ≈ 40.8 m and h ≈ 10.2 m.
¿Cómo se resuelve un problema de encuent: How is a problem about two moving bodies meeting solved?
Se escribe la posición de cada móvil (MR: Write the position of each body (uniform motion: x = x₀ + vt; uniformly accelerated: x = x₀ + v₀t + ½at²) and set them equal. If A leaves at 20 m/s and B is 100 m ahead moving at 10 m/s in the same direction, 20t = 100 + 10t, so they meet after 10 s.

Sin rozamiento el movimiento se separa e: Without friction the motion separates into two: horizontally it is uniform and vertically uniformly accelerated with $a = −g$.
$x = v_0 cos α · t$ &emsp; $y = y_0 + v_: $x = v_0 cos α · t$   $y = y_0 + v_0 sin α · t − 1/2 g t^2$
La altura máxima se alcanza cuando $v_y: The maximum height is reached when $v_y = 0$, at $t = {v_0 sin α}/g$, and equals $y_0 + {v_0^2 sin^2 α}/{2g}$. If it starts and lands at the same height, the range is $R = {v_0^2 sin 2α}/g$, maximum at 45°. Eliminating t gives the equation of the trajectory, a parabola:
Si sale desde una altura $h$ por encima: If it starts from a height $h$ above the ground, the angle of maximum range is somewhat less than 45°: $tan α = v_0/√(v_0^2 + 2gh)$. With the same $v_0$ and all possible angles, no trajectory goes above the safety parabola $y = y_0 + v_0^2/(2g) − {g x^2}/{2 v_0^2}$. Solving the trajectory equation for $v_0$ gives the speed needed to hit a target at a given angle.
Con una fuerza de rozamiento proporciona: With a friction force proportional to the velocity, $a = −g ĵ − (b/m) v$, the equations still have an exact solution with exponentials and the falling speed tends to $v_L = {m g}/b$. With quadratic drag, $a = −g ĵ − (c/m) |v| v$, which is what happens with a real ball, it has to be integrated numerically. In both cases the trajectory is no longer symmetric: it comes down steeper than it goes up.
En la gráfica x(t) la pendiente es la ve: In the x(t) graph the slope is the velocity, and in v(t) the slope is the acceleration and the area under the curve is the displacement.
Dos móviles en la misma recta se encuent: Two bodies on the same line meet when they are in the same place at the same time: $x_A(t) = x_B(t)$, a first- or second-degree equation in t.
En el MCU la velocidad angular es consta: In uniform circular motion the angular velocity is constant: $θ = ω t$, $v = ω R$, $T = 2π/ω$ and $f = 1/T$. Although the magnitude of the velocity does not change, its direction does, and there is an acceleration towards the centre, the centripetal acceleration: $a_n = ω^2 R = v^2/R$.
En el MCUA la aceleración angular α es c: In uniformly accelerated circular motion the angular acceleration α is constant: $ω = ω_0 + α t$ and $θ = ω_0 t + 1/2 α t^2$, just like uniformly accelerated rectilinear motion with x replaced by θ. There is also a tangential acceleration $a_t = α R$, and the total is $|a| = √(a_n^2 + a_t^2)$.
